title: The Hunters Hunted
timelinePosition: Same night as Chapter 7, minutes after the commitment to a same-night capture. Scene 1 runs from the lane ambush into the safe house; Scene 2 is the flight through the back streets later that night; Scene 3 is the hour after in Corin's hideout, still before dawn.
openLocation: Andorhal at night: the lane by the secondary granary loft (Hurdle Lane / Tenter Row from the Ch7 plan), then a safe house, back streets, and Corin's hideout.
transport: On foot through the city under cover and stealth. Horses are left in a carter's yard (Ch7).
immediateObjective: Take a living cultist, force the Andorhal cell to reveal who is above it, and get out before the city closes around them.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Jaina only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, feel, read or infer. She senses magic and contamination; she cannot read Sylvanas's reasons, only the shape of the calls. Havel's guilt reaches her as pattern and body, not as a narrated fact, until the escape exposes it.

Address: narration says 'Sylvanas' (Ch4 onward); aloud Jaina says 'Ranger-General'. Lyriel calls her 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not. Sylvanas aloud says 'Mage', or 'Proudmoore' in front of others. No warm trust language; the partnership shows as coverage of blind sides, never speeches.

Jaina's body (carried Ch2-7): right hand dead, left raw with two usable fingertips. She cannot write. 'Emergency notes' in B6 and the map work in B7 MUST be Corin's hand at her dictation, or Jaina working from spoken memory and spell-light marks. Her spells cost her; she is depleted going into the night, and Ch7 set up a single jaw-freeze on the target that she can do only once tonight.
No dialogue is pre-written. Prisoner and Havel speak in function (fear, evasion, procedure) only; the prisoner's half-sentence must carry the shape of a name without the name.

Do not confirm before B7 that the grain is already beyond recall. B1-B6 may hold only suspicion of reach. Do not name Kel'Thuzad before B8, not even as an unnamed 'former Council man' the narration already recognizes.

Havel: on cult coin (outline). Ch7 kept him as a harried, territorial captain with route-steering and a known 'who is on your back' formation question. Pre-B5, the narration must not state his guilt; it may let Jaina notice, and file under territorial, what the reader can see in hindsight.
Lyriel is alive at close. She dies in Ch9: no foreshadowing; her perimeter competence reads as ordinary. Cyndia and Lyriel hold flanks cleanly.

The old carter, the tally-man and the newer grain-man clue stay off the active board. Do not solve them. Do not re-stage the Ch7 B6 mechanism (packaging-stage carrier layer plus body participation); the new rung is live monitoring and the death-curse.
Do not claim the whole kingdom is lost. Do not give Kel'Thuzad's exact base. Do not assert full Barov guilt. Do not claim shutting Andorhal alone could undo the spread.

povKnowsAtOpen: Andorhal's grain is being treated at the hub before shipment; the poison goes in at packaging by skilled alchemical and necromantic hands.
The city holds a living cult network, at least eight people and two layers (handlers and contaminators), not isolated saboteurs.
Corin has been useful inside the records.
Havel keeps trying to push the work back into militia routes and shelters he controls.
Sylvanas's street read and Jaina's magical read work well enough to support a same-night ambush.
Lyriel is alive and the four-woman scouting party is intact.
Jaina's sensitivity keeps them ahead of most of the crown's awareness but not ahead of grain already moving through ordinary roads.
Brask's boy / Tam-type watchers died rather than talk (collar poison); trained men here die before they betray.
Jaina can isolate the poisoned grain magic but cannot stop the final curse that turns sickness into undeath.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Whether a captured zealot can stay alive long enough to talk.
Whether the local cult can kill compromised members from a distance.
Whether they are still early enough to slow the spread.
Who commands the operation or where that command sits.
That Havel is on cult coin.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No confirmation before B7 that the grain is already beyond recall.
No naming of Kel'Thuzad before B8.
No solution of the old carter or the newer grain-man clue.
No claim that the whole kingdom is already lost.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: The network can kill captured zealots with a death-curse from a distance.
Havel was cult-paid and dies when he tries to close the trap; Sylvanas killed him.
Corin stays inside the trust boundary and stays local when the party moves on.
Andorhal is a working hub; treated grain has already moved into northern Lordaeron.
Kel'Thuzad is identified as the former Kirin Tor mind behind the plague, operating east of Andorhal.
The party can detect the plague earlier than most authorities but is still behind the spread.

pov: She opens believing one live prisoner can give them the answer they need.
The capture works, but the witness dies before she can save him.
She learns that proof can still arrive too late to protect the person carrying it.
By the end, she has a name, but she loses the belief that clarity alone will keep them ahead.

beats: Sylvanas runs the ambush, the streets, and the escape with clean practical judgment.
Jaina trusts her field instincts now, even while she still treats magic as the cleaner road to certainty.
The death-curse shows how much the work depends on Sylvanas keeping danger physical and immediate.
Their coordination is fast enough to look effortless.

team.label: Partnership
beats: Their partnership is finally working at full speed.
Each woman covers the other's blind side before being asked.
They do not need speeches to show trust.
The cult answers that trust with a trap they barely survive.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the hunting party.
Lyriel: still with the hunting party and alive at close. She is still the one who talks to Jaina and jokes where Cyndia will not.
Corin: a real ally inside Andorhal. He stays local once the party moves on.
Captain Havel: posing as an ally at open. Exposed as a cult-paid contact and killed in the escape.
Kel'Thuzad: not yet named at chapter open.
The old carter and the newer grain-man clue: keep off the active board.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 9 opens with the same four-woman scouting party hunting east into the Eastweald.

factsLocked: The cult can kill captured zealots with a death-curse.
Havel was a cult-paid city contact, and Sylvanas kills him when he turns the trap.
Corin remains a trusted ally inside Andorhal.
Andorhal is a working hub, and treated grain has already moved into northern Lordaeron.
Kel'Thuzad is identified as the former Kirin Tor mastermind operating east of Andorhal.
The same four-woman scouting party carries the hunt forward.
factsNotEarned: An answer to the old carter and the newer grain-man clue.
Any claim that shutting down Andorhal alone can undo the spread.

scenes.title: The Capture
scenes.sceneFunction: The party takes a living cultist, gets real structure out of him, and loses him to a death-curse before he can give them the name they need.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Minutes after the decision. The target is marked, the route is chosen, and the leadership is still unnamed. Ch7 set the loft, the lane geometry (Cyndia on the roofs, Lyriel at the Tenter Row bend, Havel's lads at Hurdle Lane) and Jaina's single jaw-freeze. Jaina is depleted.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina opens believing a live prisoner is the clean answer; the scene tests that belief against the collar poison and the curse.
scenes.enrichment: Night capture in a grain-district lane: narrow cobbled lanes with warded loft doors, tallow light, grain dust in the air. Collar-poison watchers are established (Ch4 Tam/initiate). Death-curse as handler-directed monitoring follows plague-mechanism.md (Ch7-8 rung). Sources: local canon; general night-watch and safe-house practice.

beats.goal: Take a living cultist tonight, before the cell realizes it has been breached.
beats.conflict: Havel keeps steering toward shelters and corridors he controls and slower militia procedure; waiting loses the target. Wards on the loft and lane must be smothered before they flare, with the thin perimeter Ch7 set (Cyndia on the roofs over the back lane, Lyriel at the Tenter Row bend, Havel's men holding the Hurdle Lane end). The prisoner must be taken breathing, and on the move rather than at a door.

outcome.summary: They take the zealot alive and bound, and the capture is quiet, but nobody knows whether it was noticed, and Havel's lane and his offered shelter become where the man gets carried.

beats.valueShift: plan -> execution; friction-free partnership under thin cover
newOnPageInformation: The zealot is taken alive, wards smothered before they flared
Havel supplies the nearby shelter (the safe house) for questioning
Jaina and Sylvanas run a strike with no wasted movement
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the prisoner knows anything useful
sensoryAnchors: wet grain-dust on the loft sill
Lyriel and Cyndia sealing the exits
Sylvanas moving, not waiting at a door
beats.interiority: she asked for one man close enough to touch and Sylvanas brought him to her; the cold in her fingertip is the last spell she has tonight and she is not counting it; Havel's shelter is the one nobody argued with
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: the man is bound; the shelter is a minute away and the questioning has to start before the cell misses him.
beats.plannerWarning: Ch7 final set Jaina's one-time jaw-freeze (touch required) and the lane/loft geometry (hasp lock, Corin on the lock, Havel's men at Hurdle Lane). Outline says 'taking the man on the move instead of at a door'. Reconcile: he leaves the loft alone, Sylvanas takes him in the lane, Jaina's fingertip reaches his jaw. Verifier owns reshaping.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas calls the capture by event, not by clock; Jaina's contribution is touch and ward-read; Cyndia and Lyriel acknowledge in a word; Havel offers shelter as procedure; Corin on the lock only if the loft is breached.

beats.goal: Get the structure of the cell and the name of whoever is above it out of the prisoner.
beats.conflict: The man fears his masters more than his captors. Havel keeps trying to drag the questioning back to shelters, names, and procedure. Sylvanas works the man with silence rather than threat while Jaina listens for the name arriving and for any magic hovering round him.

outcome.summary: They get structure: one mortal mastermind above the cell, poisoned grain planned over months, lower-rank cultists handling the infected without understanding the full ritual. The name is nearly there and does not land.

beats.valueShift: hope of a clean answer -> a name within reach
newOnPageInformation: The operation answers upward to one mortal mastermind
Poisoned grain was planned over months

The man fears his masters more than his captors
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the prisoner will live to say it
sensoryAnchors: Jaina hearing the shape of a name
beats.interiority: she can almost hear the shape of the word and knows the shape matters; the collar was supposed to be the danger, and she took the jaw first; if she is fast enough this time
beats.transitionIntent: question-pressure: a sentence is half-built and something is about to arrive from outside the room.
beats.plannerWarning: The prisoner's fragments must later combine (B8) with Corin's local knowledge into a recognisable former-Council figure. Planner suggestion for the verifier: the half-sentence points at a title or a place of origin (a man 'out of the Citadel', a master who 'was a teacher'), never a name; invented, not outline-sourced.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas keeps the man's terror pointed at his masters; Havel's interruptions are procedural; Corin is silent in the corner or at the door; Lyriel and Cyndia hold the exits.

beats.goal: Hold the man long enough for the name to come out.
beats.conflict: A necromantic death-curse arrives from outside the room and kills him mid-sentence. Jaina feels it a breath too late: a cold needle through the room, and nothing her ward could have caught from there. The speed of the response makes the room smaller and more dangerous at once, and Havel looks worse after the curse, not better.

outcome.summary: The prisoner dies before the name; the network can kill compromised zealots from a distance, and capable cult mages are working inside the city. The safe house is now known.

newOnPageInformation: A necromantic death-curse can kill a captured zealot at range
Capable cult mages operate inside the city
The cult's response was fast and exact
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How many enforcers are already moving
beats.interiority: a faster ward might have held it; she felt it and it was already finished; what she is going to remember is the half-sentence, not the man
beats.transitionIntent: hard cut: if the cult can reach into this room, the room is already a target; Sylvanas is moving before the body settles.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas shifts from questioner to rear guard in one beat; Corin goes white; Havel's reaction is the wrong shape (he looks to the door he arrived by).

scenes.title: The Hunters Hunted
scenes.sceneFunction: The capture turns into an escape, Havel breaks open as betrayal, and the group survives only because Jaina and Sylvanas work together at speed.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The cult can kill captured zealots from a distance and now knows exactly where the investigators are.
scenes.arcPressure: The partnership works at full speed; Jaina reads magical pressure, Sylvanas reads the street, Havel is the leak neither named.
scenes.enrichment: Andorhal back streets as terrain: low walls, loading yards, granary lanes, shuttered warehouses. Local canon (lordaeron-and-northrend.md). Hideout: temporary, cramped.

beats.goal: Leave the safe house before cult enforcers close around it.
beats.conflict: Jaina reads magical pressure while Sylvanas reads streets, and they cover different danger bands in real time. Havel keeps pushing the same known routes and shelters. The cult's response is a prepared city defense, not a panic, and Havel's advice lines up too neatly with the closing net.

outcome.summary: They get out of the safe house and into the streets by a route Sylvanas picks over Havel's, and stop treating Havel as merely difficult.

beats.valueShift: trust in local help -> suspicion of Havel
newOnPageInformation: The cult has a prepared city defense
Havel's routes line up with the closing net
Jaina and Sylvanas cover different danger bands
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How wide the search ring already is
sensoryAnchors: street noise thinning in the wrong places
Sylvanas reading corners and rooflines at speed
beats.interiority: she should have seen it; she did see it, and filed it under territorial; Havel's shelters keep turning out to be the places someone is already waiting
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: the first closure is one street ahead and Havel is edging toward a route he has been selling all night.
beats.castFunction: Jaina feeds pressure-direction in few words; Sylvanas turns it into movement; Cyndia and Lyriel hold flanks wordlessly; Corin follows Jaina's staff-side.

beats.goal: Break the first closure without losing anyone and stay ahead of the steel.
beats.conflict: Jaina catches pressure shifts just before steel arrives and feeds them to Sylvanas. Havel breaks for the route he has been selling all night to close the trap. Hard turns, side alleys, rear-guard discipline.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas kills Havel with one arrow before he closes the trap; the party escapes the first closure with Corin and without Havel, with no knowledge of how much of the net he fed.

beats.valueShift: partnership as cooperation -> partnership as survival tool; Havel exposed
newOnPageInformation: Havel was in the cult's pay and tried to close the trap
Sylvanas kills him with one arrow
Corin stays with them when Havel breaks
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether any cover remains once Havel is exposed
How much of the city net he fed the cult
sensoryAnchors: one arrow settling the question of Havel
magic pressure spiking before the blades
beats.interiority: Sylvanas shot a man in the street and she is relieved, and does not look at that; the warning she gave came before the steel and Sylvanas used it without being asked
beats.transitionIntent: sensory-carry: the first closure is behind them; Corin is the only door left in the city.
beats.plannerWarning: Outline B5 requires Havel's death on the page in Jaina's POV. Keep it brief, with Jaina seeing the lamp and the arrow strike, not Sylvanas's reasoning (limited POV).
beats.castFunction: Jaina's warnings are single syllables; Sylvanas's moves anticipate them; Cyndia and Lyriel hold flanks cleanly; Corin stays with the group.

beats.emotion: Guilt and the cold of having been wrong about a man she had filed away; shaky relief at being out; the first weight of what the death-curse meant.
beats.dilemma: Keep working the Andorhal cell, which now knows them, or turn from the local cell to whatever sits above it. Whether the spread can be slowed at all is an open question.
beats.decision: She turns from the local cell to the source behind it and starts emergency notes (Corin's hand, her dictation) instead of investigation notes.
beats.goal: Fit the last pieces together in Corin's hideout.

outcome.summary: The last pieces fit: Havel's debts vanished when the supplier routes changed, reports died whenever they touched the wrong granaries, and cult enforcers moved first toward every shelter he named. The network planned for breach, containment, and witness silencing months ago. Andorhal's local cell is only one layer.

scenes.title: The Name
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina confirms the plague is already moving beyond Andorhal and finally identifies the mind behind it.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The local cult cell has shown its internal defenses, proving the group in Andorhal is only one layer of a larger problem. They are in Corin's hideout.
scenes.arcPressure: The scene tests whether Jaina's belief that clarity keeps them ahead survives the name.
scenes.enrichment: Kel'Thuzad: Council of Six archmage exiled from the Kirin Tor and Dalaran by Antonidas for necromantic work; Andorhal later served as the Cult's distribution hub (warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Kel'Thuzad; warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Andorhal). Source accounts differ on whether the expulsion was formal; outline's 'expelled' kept. Local canon: kelthuzad.md (academic, neat, lecturer), antonidas.md (trained him, failed to stop him), scholomance-and-dalaran.md (contrast rule).

beats.goal: Test whether Andorhal is the whole problem by laying her contamination map against route notes and the prisoner's last words.
beats.conflict: The lines point outward: Andorhal is a hub feeding the roads. Treated grain has already moved beyond the city and her early detection still leaves them behind. They have proof of scale but no name, and no cut-off point is in sight.

outcome.summary: The map confirms the grain has moved beyond Andorhal into northern Lordaeron; they are behind the spread, and the next answer has to come from the mind that built it.

beats.valueShift: local hope -> the sick certainty of being late
newOnPageInformation: Route lines fan outward from Andorhal
Treated grain has already moved beyond the city
Early detection still leaves them behind the spread

sensoryAnchors: route lines fanning away from Andorhal
Jaina going still over the map
beats.interiority: she has been reading the plague forward all night and it was already behind her; proof of scale arrives, and it is not the clean answer she asked for
beats.transitionIntent: question-pressure: scale without an author is only a weather report; they need a name.
beats.plannerWarning: This is the first beat allowed to confirm the grain is already beyond recall. Jaina cannot draw; Corin plots at her dictation. Do not re-stage the Ch7 B6 mechanism.
beats.castFunction: Jaina dictates, Corin plots; Sylvanas checks the roads against what she has ridden; Lyriel and Cyndia keep the door.

beats.goal: Name whoever built this, from the pieces they have.
beats.conflict: The name comes from fragments: Corin's local knowledge of a Kirin Tor scandal, the prisoner's cut-off confession, and what Havel's betrayal says about the level of planning. Corin says it as if it burns. The name is one Jaina has to carry personally.

outcome.summary: The mind behind the plague is Kel'Thuzad, a former Kirin Tor mage expelled by Antonidas for necromantic work, operating east of Andorhal. Exact base unknown. The hunt becomes personal.

beats.castFunction: Corin says the name, not Jaina; Sylvanas asks one practical question about the man; Lyriel and Cyndia read Jaina's silence.

beats.emotion: Recognition: the architect came out of the same arcane world that trained her.
beats.dilemma: Say plainly what the name means to her and risk the party's trust in her read, or carry it alone.
beats.decision: She commits to the eastbound hunt for the seat of the work; the investigation now has a familiar human center.
beats.goal: Face what the name means and point the hunt east.

outcome.summary: Jaina faces what the name means and the trail points east into the Eastweald; Chapter 9 begins as a hunt for the real seat of the work.

warnings: B1: Ch7 final set a loft door, hasp lock, and Jaina's one-time touch-based jaw-freeze; the outline says 'on the move instead of at a door'. Reconciled in the plan; verifier to confirm.
B2/B8: prisoner's fragments must carry the shape of a name without the name; fragment content is a planner suggestion, not outline-sourced.
B3/B4: how the cult locates the safe house unspecified; suggested that Havel supplied the shelter (explains exposure and fair-plays the betrayal).
B6/B7: Jaina cannot write; Corin scribes at her dictation. 'Emergency notes' and map work depend on this.
B6: the outline says Corin's 'hideout' while the interrogation was in a 'safe house'; two locations kept distinct.
Outline 'Active cast at close' lists Corin as active while 'Cast and handoff' says he stays local; plan keeps Corin at close and flags the exit for Ch9.
B6-B9 are a static hideout stretch of four beats; vary motion. Verifier owns pacing.
B5 Havel's death: limited POV means Jaina sees the arrow's effect, not Sylvanas's decision.
